name: Supabase
look: White canvas, single emerald accent, composited product screenshots, tight technical radii.

hero.title: Build in a weekend. Scale to millions.
hero.sub: Stratum is a Postgres database with authentication, storage, realtime subscriptions and edge functions attached. No lock-in, because underneath it is just Postgres.

features.title: Everything attached to your database
features.sub: Each piece works on its own. Together they are a backend you did not have to assemble.

items.title: Postgres database
items.body: A dedicated Postgres instance with extensions enabled, point-in-time recovery and no proprietary query layer in front of it.

items.title: Authentication
items.body: Email, magic links, phone and twenty OAuth providers, enforced at the row through Postgres policies.

items.title: Storage
items.body: S3-compatible object storage with image transformation on the fly and the same policy engine as the database.

items.title: Realtime
items.body: Subscribe to inserts, updates and deletes over websockets, filtered by the same row-level rules.

items.title: Edge functions
items.body: Deno functions deployed to the edge, close to your users and next to your data.

items.title: Vector search
items.body: pgvector built in, so embeddings live beside the rows they describe instead of in a second database.

showcases.title: Authorisation in the database, not the API
showcases.body: Policies are written in SQL and enforced by Postgres itself. A misconfigured client cannot read what a policy forbids, because the check happens below the API rather than inside it.
points: Enforced for REST, realtime and storage alike
Testable with a plain SQL test suite

showcases.title: It is just Postgres underneath
showcases.body: Take a pg_dump and leave whenever you like. The platform adds extensions and services around a standard database rather than replacing it with something you cannot export.

gallery.title: Documentation and examples
gallery.sub: Reference implementations for the frameworks and runtimes people actually use.

testimonial.quote: We evaluated four backends and picked the one we could walk away from. Two years later we have not needed to, which is rather the point.
testimonial.name: Tomas Berg

pricing.title: Predictable pricing, no surprises
pricing.sub: Start free. Scale when you need to. Every plan runs on dedicated Postgres.

items.a: Yes. You get a connection string to a standard Postgres instance. Everything the platform adds is built with extensions and services around it, so pg_dump gets you out cleanly.

items.q: What happens if a project is idle?
items.a: Free-tier projects pause after a week without activity and can be restored from the dashboard in about a minute. Paid projects never pause.
The core platform is Apache 2.0 licensed and there is a documented Docker Compose setup. Some managed conveniences — the dashboard's log explorer in particular — are cloud-only.
Daily backups on Pro with seven-day retention, and point-in-time recovery to any second within the retention window as an add-on.

cta.title: Start your project
cta.sub: A new Postgres database in about two minutes. Free tier, no card required.

footer.tagline: An open source backend built on Postgres.

notes: The emerald is the only chromatic event on the page. Everything else is a greyscale ladder from hairline to ink.
Composited product UI screenshots — dashboard, SQL editor, log stream — are the only decorative element. No photography, no illustration.
Button radii stay tight at 6–8px. Nothing in this system is a pill.
Code blocks sit on a near-black surface with monospace inline code; the developer DNA should be visible on every marketing surface.
The featured pricing tier inverts to near-black rather than turning green — the green stays reserved for buttons and dot accents.
